name: palette-baseline
symbols_from_why: Runs against the PINNED BASE ROM: every symbol it reads is vanilla.
description: Doc 67 slate item E, PRE-BUILD MEASUREMENT. A pure OBSERVATION spec in the shape of reps-rtc-spike.json: it asserts almost nothing on purpose, because its job is to print what a stock overworld's OBJ palette table actually holds. Item E was written against doc 47 sec.13.2's quote of the engine's own comment -- 12 of 16 slots pre-committed to a fixed PALSLOT_* scheme, two 'special' NPCs unable to coexist. Reading the pin says that scheme is DEAD CODE at this pin: InitObjectEventPalettes has no callers, sObjectPaletteTagSets and gReflectionEffectPaletteMap are read only from inside it, and graphicsInfo->paletteSlot is written in 36 data rows and read NOWHERE. Object event palettes are allocated dynamically by TAG through LoadSpritePalette/IndexOfSpritePaletteTag, first-fit from gReservedSpritePaletteCount to 15. This spec measures the consequence: how many of the 16 slots a normal overworld is actually using, and what gReservedSpritePaletteCount is when nothing has reserved anything. Run against the STOCK ENGINE -- no fork exists yet and none is needed, because every probe names an engine global (doc 68's rule: an experiment that only reads is free).

probes.why: gReservedSpritePaletteCount. IndexOfSpritePaletteTag scans from THIS index to 15, so it is the floor of the dynamic allocator. FreeAndReserveObjectSpritePalettes would set it to OBJ_PALSLOT_COUNT (12), but its only live caller is player_pc.c -- so the overworld's value is the question, not a known.
sSpritePaletteTags[0]. TAG_NONE (0x11FF at this pin's OBJ_EVENT_PAL_TAG_NONE, or 0xFFFF for the sprite-system TAG_NONE) means the slot is free.
sSpritePaletteTags[12]. The vanilla comment says slots 12-15 belong to field effects and the interface. If the allocator is genuinely first-fit from 0, that claim is also stale.

sSpritePaletteTags[15]. THE ONE THAT MATTERS. LoadSpritePalette returns 0xFF when every slot is taken, CreateSprite assigns that into oam.paletteNum, and oam.paletteNum is a 4-BIT field -- so 0xFF truncates to 15. An NPC past the budget does not vanish; it renders in whatever this slot holds.
Doc 66's rule -- assert that the thing under test actually happened. A palette table read outside the overworld is a measurement of a different screen.

assert.why: The only load-bearing assertion here. Everything else is an observation.
